summary: Integration lane (final). The merged tree of all seven phase 3-5 lanes passed scripts/test-search.sh --force with Docker on the first run: build, clippy --all-targets -D warnings for every search crate plus rolld and roll-cli, every cargo test, the dashboard helper tests, both YAML suites at their thresholds, the differential suite, the client matrix, the Postgres fleet tests and cfn-lint. Nothing broke where the lanes met. The full cargo suite also ran 3 times in a row with no failures, so no flaky tests showed up. The final benchmarks on a quiet host found one regression the lanes had introduced: std::thread::available_parallelism re-reads cgroup files on every call, and the search path called it several times per request, making it 28% of a size:0 search's CPU. It is now looked up once (search_index::search::pool::cores()). Server CPU went 0.50 -> 0.24 ms for a size:0 search and 1.57 -> 1.23 ms for a 10-hit match. test-search.sh --force is green again after the fix, and the ES YAML threshold is raised to 3809. Final benchmarks: roll wins all 17 micro rows (1.4-4.9x wall, 2.1-7.8x server CPU) and every Rally http_logs query task, with indexing at par. On Rally geonames it wins every task except two script scores and loads 1.5x faster. Updated: docs/benchmarks/search.md, the Performance section and differential table of docs/search/compatibility.md, docs/search/handoff/README.md (state table, test status, what this round did, Next phases), and contracts.md (pool::cores). This round's lane reports were copied into docs/search/handoff/<key>.json.
public_api: New: search_index::search::pool::cores() -> usize. It returns the process's usable CPUs, looked up once through a OnceLock. Use it instead of std::thread::available_parallelism() on any per-request path; this is documented in contracts.md under search-index. No other public API changed.

notes_for_others: Never call std::thread::available_parallelism() per request: it reads cgroup files every time. Use search_index::search::pool::cores(). Per-segment-write call sites in search-codec (writer.rs, bp.rs) still call it, which is negligible there.

On a quiet host, a sequential client's wall time includes waking sleeping cores, so the micro suite's query rows show 0.3-0.5 ms more wall than on the busy host of earlier rounds even when CPU per request is lower. Compare server CPU (the micro suite's cgroup table) when A/B testing.
In shell commands, write the loopback address literally (127.0.0.1). The redacted '[IP]' placeholder in summaries breaks docker -p, --listen and Python URLs.
pkill -f with a pattern that also appears in your own command line kills your shell. Kill benchmark servers by PID.
